retrieval.answer: According to the Verta tariff schedule, the standard Tier 3 FX spread is **0.5%**, applied over the mid-market rate once the free monthly conversion allowance is exhausted. The total free monthly conversion allowance for Tier 3 is **EUR 5,000**.

searches.query: Tier 3 FX spread after free allowance exhausted monthly free conversion allowance

fragments.text:
Verta tariff schedule
## FX spreads by tier
The spread is applied over the mid-market rate only after the free monthly
conversion allowance is exhausted.

| Tier | FX spread | Free monthly conversion allowance |
|---|---|---|
| Tier 1 | 1.5% | EUR 500 |
| Tier 2 | 0.9% | EUR 1,000 |
| Tier 3 | 0.5% | EUR 5,000 |

Currency conversion guide
## How a conversion is priced
A conversion quote has these components, in order: the mid-market rate for the
currency pair; the tier spread (a percentage of the gross converted amount);
the free monthly conversion allowance. If the whole conversion fits within the
customer's remaining monthly allowance, no spread is charged. Once the
allowance is exhausted, the full tier spread applies to the conversion.

Onboarding and tiers
## Tier benefits
A higher tier lowers the FX spread, raises the free monthly conversion
allowance and raises both transfer limits.

Currency conversion operations
## Allowance accounting
The free monthly conversion allowance is counted in EUR equivalent and resets on
the first calendar day of each month. Allowance consumption is recorded at
settlement. A conversion that would cross the allowance boundary has the tier
spread applied to the entire conversion, not only to the portion above the
boundary.

retrieval.answer: The Verta tariff schedule lists the flat fee for a SEPA transfer as **EUR 0.35**, with a 0% percentage fee.

searches.query: fixed EUR fee for a SEPA transfer

fragments.text:
Verta tariff schedule
## Transfer fees by type
| Transfer type | Flat fee | Percentage fee |
|---|---|---|
| Internal | EUR 0.00 | 0% |
| SEPA | EUR 0.35 | 0% |
| SWIFT | EUR 15.00 | 0.3% |
| Card payment | EUR 0.00 | 1.2% |

The percentage fee is calculated on the EUR equivalent of the transfer amount.

Fee details
## Card payment fee
Card payments carry a percentage fee on the EUR equivalent. No flat fee
applies.

Fee details
## How the SWIFT fee is composed
A SWIFT transfer carries a flat fee plus a percentage of the EUR equivalent of
the amount sent. Correspondent bank charges deducted en route are outside the
control of Verta and are not refunded.

Escalation policy
## Mandatory escalation triggers
The agent must escalate to a human agent when: suspected fraud is reported on a
settled transaction above EUR 10,000; the customer explicitly asks for a human;
the request needs an action the agent has no tool for; a dispute is blocked by a
customer-level restriction; the customer disputes a figure the agent quoted.

The Verta dispute documentation gives the reason code **goods_not_received** a chargeback window of **90 days**, counted from the transaction date.

Under the eligibility conditions in the same document, a dispute is only eligible if the transaction date is still within that window relative to the current date.

searches.query: goods_not_received dispute window days from transaction date

fragments.text:
Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Glossary
## Chargeback window
The number of days, counted from the transaction date, during which a dispute
may be raised under a given reason code.

Limit operations
## Window definition
Limits are tracked on calendar days, not business days. The daily window runs
from 00:00 to 23:59 CET.

Payment dispute rules
## Eligibility conditions
A dispute is eligible only if all of the following hold: the reason code is
valid; the transaction status is settled; the transaction date is within the
reason code's window relative to the current date; and no customer-level
restriction applies (for example, an account under compliance review cannot
open new disputes until the review concludes).
